issues.legal_issue: A landlord who is an undivided co-owner of premises is an owner for the purpose of seeking eviction on the ground of reasonable requirement for personal occupation.
material_facts: The plaintiff was the acknowledged landlord and a co-owner of the premises, which had not been partitioned.
The premises were found reasonably required for occupation by the plaintiff and members of his joint family.
The tenant argued that the plaintiff had to be the absolute owner to obtain eviction.
issues.conclusion: A co-owner who is also the acknowledged landlord is an owner within the meaning of the applicable eviction provision; sole ownership need not be established.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 13(1)(f) of the West Bengal Premises Tenancy Act, 1956, a landlord seeking eviction for his own occupation must be an owner, but an undivided co-owner meets that requirement. Co-ownership vests the whole property in each co-owner jointly; a co-owner does not own merely a fractional physical part unless partition occurs. The Court relied on the account of co-ownership in Salmond on Jurisprudence.

rule.if: eviction_proceeding and personal_occupation_ground and plaintiff_is_landlord and plaintiff_is_co_owner and property_is_unpartitioned

predicates.eviction_proceeding: A landlord brought a proceeding seeking eviction of a tenant.
predicates.personal_occupation_ground: The landlord sought eviction on the ground that the premises were reasonably required for personal occupation.
predicates.plaintiff_is_landlord: The person seeking eviction was acknowledged to be the tenant's landlord.
predicates.plaintiff_is_co_owner: The landlord held ownership of the premises jointly with other co-owners.
predicates.property_is_unpartitioned: The co-owners' interests in the premises had not been separated by partition.

issues.definition: When an eviction proceeding rests on reasonable personal occupation and an acknowledged landlord holds the unpartitioned property jointly with others, that landlord meets the owner requirement.

issues.legal_issue: An objection that an eviction suit is improperly framed for failure to join other co-owners must be raised at the earliest opportunity.
material_facts: The tenant argued that all co-owners should have been joined as plaintiffs.
The objection to the suit's framing was not raised at the earliest opportunity and was pressed in the Supreme Court.
issues.conclusion: The objection to non-joinder could not be accepted because it had not been raised at the earliest opportunity.
issues.legal_principle: An objection concerning the frame of a suit, including an objection that other co-owners should have been joined, should be raised at the earliest opportunity.

predicates.eviction_suit: A landlord brought a suit seeking eviction of a tenant.
predicates.nonjoinder_objection: A party objected that other co-owners had not been joined in the suit.
predicates.objection_not_raised_at_earliest_opportu: The party did not raise the objection at the earliest opportunity.

issues.definition: In an eviction suit, a non-joinder objection raised later than the earliest opportunity is rejected as untimely.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant in a landlord-tenant suit is estopped from denying that the landlord had title to the premises when the tenancy began.
material_facts: The relationship between the parties was that of landlord and tenant.
The plaintiff was acknowledged by the defendants to be their landlord and was a co-owner of the premises.
The tenant disputed the plaintiff's entitlement to sue by arguing that other co-owners had not joined.
issues.conclusion: The tenant could not question the landlord's title at the commencement of the tenancy, and title to the leased property was irrelevant to the landlord-tenant suit.
issues.legal_principle: Section 116 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, estops a tenant from denying that the landlord had title to the premises at the commencement of the tenancy. Under the general law, title to the leased property is irrelevant in a suit between landlord and tenant.

predicates.landlord_tenant_suit: A landlord brought a suit against a tenant concerning the tenancy.
predicates.landlord_recognized_by_tenant: The tenant recognized the person bringing suit as the landlord.
predicates.tenant_denies_title_at_tenancy_start: The tenant disputed that the landlord had title when the tenancy began.

issues.definition: In a suit between a recognized landlord and tenant, a tenant who disputes the landlord's title at the start of the tenancy is estopped from that denial.

issues.legal_issue: A landlord's reasonable personal-occupation requirement may be supported by the need of a family member or dependent, without requiring every co-owner to have a separate personal need.
material_facts: The premises were reasonably required for occupation by members of the landlord's joint family, including his mother and married brother.
The landlord's family lived together, and the existing accommodation was found inadequate for the family.
The tenant contended that the requirements of all the landlords or co-owners had to be established.
issues.conclusion: The reasonable requirement of any one family member or dependent may furnish a ground for eviction on personal-requirement grounds; the requirement need not be that of every co-owner.
issues.legal_principle: In applying the personal-occupation part of section 13(1)(f) of the West Bengal Premises Tenancy Act, 1956, the Court rejected the English approach in Mclntyre v. Hardcastle, under which the requirement of all landlords was necessary. It approved the approach in Kanika Devi v. Amarendra Nath Roy Choudhury, Tarak Chandra Mukherjee v. Ratanlal Ghosal, Taherbhai Hebtullabhai v. Ambalal Harilal Shah, and Deb Ranjan Chatterjee v. Swarnarani Biswas: the reasonable requirement of any one family member or dependent can support eviction.

rule.if: eviction_proceeding and personal_occupation_ground and family_member_or_dependent_needs_premises and need_is_reasonable

predicates.eviction_proceeding: A landlord brought a proceeding seeking eviction of a tenant.
predicates.personal_occupation_ground: The landlord relied on reasonable requirement for personal occupation as the ground for eviction.
predicates.family_member_or_dependent_needs_premise: A family member or dependent needed the premises for occupation.
predicates.need_is_reasonable: The need for the premises was found to be reasonable.

issues.definition: In an eviction proceeding based on reasonable personal occupation, a reasonable need of a family member or dependent can support eviction.
